subject: SEM degress of freedom (direct effects model vs. fully mediated model)

messages.author: bd7efbeddbcc7d48
messages.subject: SEM degress of freedom (direct effects model vs. fully mediated model)
parts:
Hi,

I have two different models.

The first model includes only direct effects:
y ~ x1 + x2 + m1 + m2

The second model includes direct effects and mediated effects:
y ~ x1 + x2 + m1 + m2
m1 ~ x1
m2 ~ x2

I am confused by the degrees of freedom (df). The first model has 0 df. The second model has 3 df.
I would expect the first model to have 5 df because the model has two more free paths compared with the second model.

I think the problem is that the first model treats m1 and m2 as exogenous variables.
If I add the following lines to the first model, I get 5 df:
m1 ~ 1*m1
m2 ~ 1*m2
Is this correct?

Thank you in advance.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: SEM degress of freedom (direct effects model vs. fully mediated model)
parts:
Yes. I'm guessing you're using sem() and not lavaan().

In the first model, sem() implicitly adds covariances between all of the predictors.i.e.
x1 ~~ x2
x1 ~~ m1
etc.
So you have 4 regression paths, and 6 covariances in the model.

IN the second model, m1 and m2 are no longer exogenous, so they are not correlated automatically (that's 1 df - you should add it).

The covariance between m1 and x1 has been replaced with a regression, as has m2 and x2. But the crossovers - x1~~m2 and x2~~ x1 have not been replaced. That's your other two, making three.

Jeremy

It may help if you look at the output of

parTable(fit)

for the various models. There you can an overview of the model
parameters (some of which are added automatically to the model if you
are using the sem() function).
